Exercise 10 · Example. Paper newspapers lose readers, and digital subscriptions do not compensate for losses. A report from the publishing association reveals that distributed copies of paper newspapers have dropped by 60% in ten years, and that three newspapers have ceased their publications only in the last year. On the other hand, the number of subscribers to digital editions has increased, but subscription revenues cover only a small part of the advertising losses, mostly ended up on social platforms and search engines. The director of one of the major newspapers said that his newspaper was forced to fire a quarter of the journalists, adding: "We produce news, and platforms collect profits." The association calls for a law that obliges large platforms to pay a fee for the media content they spread. According to some researchers, the future of journalism will not be just paper or digital, but will depend on "trust": according to a recent study, readers are willing to pay for a journalism they trust, not for the news as such, which they find free everywhere.
